headline: Broad Rally Holds Mid-Session as Semis Lead and Corsair Surges 33%
body_html:
Stocks are holding firm through the midday hour on Friday, with advancers outpacing decliners by a commanding margin of roughly 396 to 152 across the tracked universe. Semiconductors are pacing all sectors, up 3.34% on the session, followed by Software at 1.97% and Materials at 1.83%. The tone is constructive even as traders keep one eye on the afternoon's U.S. jobs report, a release that has kept positioning cautious in the options market all week.

The day's dominant narrative is earnings-driven dispersion. Corsair Gaming is the session's undisputed standout, rocketing 32.83% after results that surprised the street. Twilio is close behind, surging 22.85% on strong communications-platform numbers. On the other side, Trade Desk is cratering 24.36%, a punishing reversal that is weighing on the broader ad-tech complex even as DoubleVerify rallies nearly 13% in the same space. The split underscores how unforgiving the tape has been for any company that misses on revenue guidance.

Into the close, the key watch points are the jobs print and any developments in Iran-Oman talks, with oil already sliding on reports of a potential Hormuz agreement. Energy is the lone sector in the red, off 0.54%, reflecting that headline risk directly. A soft payrolls number could extend the rally; a hot one may test it.

briefs.headline: Corsair Gaming Explodes Higher on Surprise Earnings Beat
briefs.body: Corsair Gaming shares are up nearly 33% mid-session, making the gaming-hardware maker the undisputed standout of the day. Results cleared street expectations by a wide margin, triggering a wave of short-covering and fresh buying. The move is one of the sharpest single-session gains in the company's recent history.

briefs.headline: Trade Desk Plunges as Ad-Tech Divide Widens
briefs.body: Trade Desk is tumbling 24.36%, one of the steepest declines in the tracked universe, after its quarterly results disappointed on forward revenue guidance. The drop stands in sharp contrast to DoubleVerify's 12.94% advance, highlighting a stark split in investor confidence across the digital-advertising technology landscape.

briefs.headline: Hormuz Tension Eases, Dragging Oil and Energy Stocks Lower
briefs.body: Oil prices are retreating as reports of Iran-Oman diplomatic contacts raise hopes for a potential agreement to restore vessel traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. Energy is the only sector trading in negative territory on the session, sliding 0.54%. Innovex International, an oil-services name, is among the day's steeper decliners, off 7.84%.

briefs.headline: Dollar Heads for Weekly Gain Ahead of Afternoon Jobs Data
briefs.body: The greenback is on pace to close the week higher as traders balance Iran-related geopolitical risk against the prospect of a firm U.S. payrolls print. The afternoon jobs release is being watched as a potential catalyst for a reassessment of Federal Reserve rate expectations, keeping bond markets unsettled into the final hours.

briefs.headline: Gold Poised for Best Weekly Advance Since January
briefs.body: Bullion is set to record its strongest weekly performance since the start of the year, supported by receding inflation fears and safe-haven demand tied to Middle East uncertainty. The metal has attracted steady inflows throughout the week, with geopolitical headlines around Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan adding a security-premium bid.

briefs.headline: White House Courts Mining Industry in Push for Defense Minerals
briefs.body: The Trump administration is convening mining executives at the White House as officials seek to shore up domestic and allied supplies of critical minerals for defense supply chains. The outreach comes as Homebuilders and Materials sectors both post strong mid-session gains of 1.70% and 1.83% respectively, reflecting broader industrial-policy optimism.
